verdict.summary: GitHub OAuth apps are registered in a form with no documented review step. The friction is organization approval of your app, not GitHub review. Review applies only if you list on Marketplace.

gates.name: Registered OAuth app, your own account
gates.unlocks: Connect your own GitHub account through your app.
limits: Max 100 OAuth apps per user or organization

gates.name: Other users and organizations (unlisted app)
gates.unlocks: Other users can authorize the app for personal-account access. Organization resources require owner approval where access restrictions apply.
limits: No GitHub-published user or install cap found for unlisted apps
New organizations have OAuth app access restrictions on by default; owners must approve the app
Members can still use unapproved apps for personal-account access
2,000 access-token requests per hour per app
Same user signing in 10 times in an hour must re-authorize
Calls count against each user's 5,000/hour REST limit
Private or internal apps only allow sign-in by members of the owning org or enterprise
Expiring user tokens by default: 8-hour access token, 6-month unused refresh token
gates.time_to_reach: Same day; depends on org owners approving

gates.name: Anyone, plus optional Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Public installs need no GitHub review. A Marketplace listing adds discovery and, for organization-owned apps, paid plans.
limits: Review applies only to Marketplace listings
Listing needs a publisher contact, description, pricing plan, privacy policy link and support link
App must add value beyond sign-in and be publicly available
Paid plans need 200+ users, an organization-owned verified publisher, and purchase webhook handling
Only org owners can submit an org-owned app's listing
gates.time_to_reach: Public use: immediate. Marketplace: roughly 1-6 weeks (community-reported, no SLA).

steps.title: Decide: managed auth or your own app
steps.detail: Composio's managed GitHub app uses broad default scopes (repo, user, gist, notifications, project, workflow, codespace). Register your own app if you need narrower scopes, your own app identity, or your own callback URL. GitHub also recommends considering a GitHub App instead of an OAuth app.

steps.title: Get the Composio callback URL
steps.detail: Create a GitHub auth config in Composio with custom credentials and copy the callback URL it shows.

steps.title: Open the OAuth Apps page
steps.detail: Sign in and go to profile menu > Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps > New OAuth App. For an organization-owned app, use the organization's settings, which requires admin access.

steps.title: Fill in the registration form
steps.detail: Enter Application name, Homepage URL and an optional description. Paste the Composio callback URL as the Authorization callback URL.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Up to 10 callback URLs can be added.
If redirect_uri is sent, its host and port must match a registered callback and its path must be under it.

steps.title: Choose token expiry setting
steps.detail: Expire user access tokens is on by default. Leave it on if your client refreshes tokens. Otherwise clear it, noting that enabling it later affects only newly issued tokens.
gotchas: Expiring tokens last 8 hours; refresh tokens expire after 6 months unused, and a refresh returns a new pair.

steps.title: Register and copy credentials
steps.detail: Click Register application, then generate a client secret and copy the client ID and secret. Enter them in your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Pick scopes and test your own connection
steps.detail: Request only the scopes you need. Run an authorization with your own account, using the state parameter (PKCE is also supported), and confirm the token works.
gotchas: Users can narrow scopes on the consent screen, so handle receiving fewer scopes than requested.
Scopes never grant more than the user already has.

steps.title: Get organization approval where needed
steps.detail: For users who need your app to reach organization resources, an org owner must approve it after a member requests it. Org owners may also have disabled app requests.
gotchas: Private or internal apps only let members of the owning org or enterprise sign in.

steps.title: Plan for rate limits and device flow
steps.detail: Keep token requests under 2,000 per hour and avoid repeated sign-ins. If you use device flow, enable it in app settings first.
gotchas: Device flow user-code submissions are limited to 50 per hour per app.

steps.title: Optionally list on GitHub Marketplace
steps.detail: Not needed for public use. If you want a listing, prepare a privacy policy link, support contact, description and pricing plan. An org owner then clicks Request publish on the listing Overview page.
gotchas: Paid plans need 200+ users and a verified org publisher.

steps.title: Wait for Marketplace onboarding
steps.detail: An onboarding expert contacts you after submission. GitHub states no timeline. Community reports range from 1 to 6 weeks, and those reports are about GitHub Apps listings.

requirements.item: GitHub account (personal, or org admin access)
requirements.detail: You can register under a personal account or any organization where you have admin access.
The form requires an application name, homepage URL and callback URL.

requirements.item: Org owner approval for org data
requirements.detail: Organizations with access restrictions need an owner to approve the app.
Privacy policy link, support link, description, pricing plan, publicly available app, value beyond sign-in. Paid plans also need 200+ users and a verified org publisher.

scopes.effect: High-impact scope. The docs read note no review gate. It appears on the user's consent screen.
Lets the token add and update GitHub Actions workflow files. No review gate documented.
Marked high-impact in the scope table. No review gate documented.
Requesting it gives an expiring token and refresh token for a single sign-in even if the app setting is off.

blockers.symptom: Organization members cannot authorize your app against org resources
blockers.cause: OAuth app access restrictions are on by default for new organizations.
blockers.fix: Have a member request the app, then an org owner approves it. Members can still use the app for personal-account access.

blockers.symptom: Sign-in forces re-authorization or new tokens are blocked
blockers.cause: Rate limits: 10 sign-ins per user per hour, or over 2,000 token requests per hour.
blockers.fix: Reuse and refresh tokens rather than re-running the flow. Wait for the limit window to pass.

blockers.cause: Limit of 50 user-code submissions per hour per app.
blockers.fix: Reduce code submissions and retry later.

blockers.cause: Expiring user tokens are on by default for new apps.
blockers.fix: Implement refresh token exchange, or clear Expire user access tokens in app settings.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed app to test quickly, but its default scopes are broad. Register your own OAuth app if you need narrower scopes, your own app identity or your own callback URL. Enter the Composio callback URL from your auth config as the callback URL either way. Registration is self-serve with no documented review.

open_questions: No GitHub-published install or user cap for unlisted OAuth apps was found; only rate limits and org controls.
No official OAuth app review process was found; self-serve registration is inferred from the creation page.
Marketplace review timelines come only from community threads about GitHub Apps listings; GitHub publishes no SLA.
Whether GitHub screens OAuth scope requests beyond the consent screen is not documented.
The 2026 refresh-token changelog was read only through search snippets.
